chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) was brought an unmarried girl who had stolen, so he lashed her with a whip and did not cut her.

key_terms.قَطَعَ: to cut (specifically amputation of the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for theft by an unmarried girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the lesser punishment of flogging (*darb*) and the major *hadd* penalty of hand amputation (*qat'*) for a young girl who committed theft. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the strict physical mutilation of the *hadd* is often suspended for minors or those lacking full legal capacity, even if they are held accountable for the act through disciplinary flogging. It serves as a key precedent for understanding the flexibility of *hadd* punishments when applied to children or young women in early Islamic legal practice.
